The principal aim of this Act is to make it a legal or
statutory obligation for any firm or individual, among others,
havir,g a place c,f business and carrying on business in Kiribati
under a business name which does not consist, among other thlngs,
of the true surnames of all partners (in the case of firms) or
the true surname (in the case of an individual) to be registered
in the manner described in the Act,
Sections 4 and 5 of the Act specify the firms and persons
re~uired to be registered under the Act and the manner and part­
culars of registration, Sections9and 12 impose·penalties for·
default in registration and for false statements. Furthermore,
Section 19 empowers the Minister to make regulations prescribing,
arnong other things, fees payable under the Act and anything
desirable for the better carr,Jing into effect the provisions of
the Act. It is to be noted that apart from the prescribed fees
payable under Section 16. of the Act for inspection and making of
copies or extracts of certificates of registration or statements
filed with the Registrar of Business names, no fees are imposed
under the .Act.
At present, with the exception of companies incorporated under
the Companies Ordinance (Cap. iOA), Government has no readily
available source of information as to the number of individual
persons or firms carrying on business under various names and
styles, The types of business being carried on under such names
and styles are also not readily known to Governmerlt.
This Act, on passage into law, will therefore serve as an
instrument for gathering useful statistical and other data needed
for Government planning and monitoring. It may also enable
Government, among other things, to widen the tax net to include
certain individuals and firms who or which derive substantial
income from various types of bµs:ineSs but who or which are not
taxed because of the difficulty in identifying them.
The legislation envisaged by this Act will not be peculiar
to Kiribati, !llost countries (both developed and developing)
have similar legislation and it is to be emp~sised that only
businesses being carried on under business names (i.e. names
other than .their corporate names or p±oprietors' names) are
affected by this proposed legislation,
